title: Prove approval-required policy blocks production module-backed Skills
goal: Verify the production M8 chat-to-Skill-to-Module path refuses a module-backed Skill when the injected live policy requires explicit approval, without executing the underlying tool.
context: SkillRuntime and ModuleRuntime already fail closed on approval-required decisions, and existing unit coverage checks approval for the built-in text normalizer. Issue #347 requires evidence on the production module-backed path as well, where workspace Skills resolve through ToolModule and ModuleRuntime.
forbidden_changes: Do not treat approval-required as an implicit grant or weaken the production policy boundary.
Do not change executor mappings, workspace scope/path validation, or runtime policy behavior.
Do not modify UI, provider/GGUF, or unrelated tests.
acceptance_criteria: An M8 workspace Skill selected from chat throws the typed module-policy failure when Skill policy allows but Module policy requires approval.
The regression exercises the module-backed production mapping with workspace tools enabled.
The event log proves the Module is failed and never invoked.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If the test reveals a policy bypass, fix only the failing production boundary and retain explicit approval semantics; if setup is invalid, repair the fixture rather than weakening the assertion.
